name: ints_abs
reduction: a.abs() returns the receiver unchanged; .abs() is a no-op in the derived frontend (unknown method passes receiver through). Same root as pow/min/max/saturating_add.

name: ints_pow
reduction: a.pow(40) returns receiver (2) unchanged; pow method unimplemented, treated as identity on receiver.

name: ints_min_max
reduction: a.min(b)/a.max(b) return receiver a(=5) => prints 5; min/max unimplemented (identity on receiver).

name: ints_saturating
reduction: a.saturating_add(100) returns receiver (200) unchanged; saturating_add unimplemented (identity on receiver).

name: ints_checked_none
reduction: checked_add value does not match the None arm as rustc does; match prints nothing. Option-returning checked_* arithmetic unsupported.

name: ints_hex_bin_oct
reduction: 0xff parses (255) but 0b1010 and 0o17 contribute 0; binary/octal literal prefixes mis-lexed to 0. Reduce: println!("{}",0b1010) => 0 instead of 10.

name: ints_i64_cast_i32

name: ints_i8_neg_cast

name: ints_signed_shr

name: ints_u64_big
reduction: u64::MAX literal truncated to 32 bits; pervasive 32-bit value model. Reduce: println!("{}",4294967296u64) => 0.

name: ints_overflow_add
reduction: rustc rejects the const-evaluable overflow at compile time even under -O; derived accepts and runs, printing a truncated value. Frontend does no const-overflow check.

name: slices_arr_sum

name: slices_contains

name: slices_windows

name: slices_chunks

name: slices_sort

name: slices_sort_by

name: slices_split_at

name: vecmeth_sortbykey

name: vecmeth_drain
reduction: v.drain(1..3) yields a garbage pointer sum and does not remove elements; drain range unimplemented.

name: vecmeth_itermut
reduction: for x in v.iter_mut() { *x *= 10 } segfaults (exit 139, no output); iter_mut mutable deref-store unsupported.

name: vecmeth_firstlast
reduction: first()/last() unwrap returns garbage pointer instead of element value 7/9.

name: vecmeth_isempty

name: patterns_or_mismatch
reduction: Both reject E::A(n)|E::B(_); derived's diagnostic is non-exhaustive rather than the true 'variable not bound in all patterns', but rejection is correct.

name: patterns_or_variant
reduction: Minimal: `match v { E::A(n) | E::B(n) => n, E::C(n) => n+1 }`. Derived does not treat a single variant-spanning or-arm as covering both variants, so exhaustiveness check fails. Frontend models or-patterns per-alternative but loses that both A and B are matched by one arm.

name: patterns_nested_enum
reduction: `match W::X(E::B(7)) { W::X(E::B(n)) => n, ... }` binds nothing usable: derived runs but println emits empty. Nested variant-in-variant destructure fails to extract the inner payload n; the value threaded to println is wrong/empty.

name: patterns_at_nested
feature: @ binding nested inside enum variant E::N(x @ 1..=10)
reduction: `E::N(x @ 1..=10) => x*3` — same class as nested_enum: an @ binding one level inside a variant pattern doesn't bind; println prints empty. Combines @-binding with nested destructure.

name: patterns_ref_binding
reduction: `match v.first() { Some(&n) => n+sum, ... }` — the by-reference sub-pattern Some(&n) fails to bind n (the dereferenced value); output empty. Reference-destructuring patterns unsupported/miscompiled.

name: patterns_ref_mut
feature: ref mut binding mutating through pattern
reduction: `match n { ref mut x => *x += 10 }` then print n. Derived prints 5 (unchanged) vs 15: the `ref mut x` binding does not alias the scrutinee, so `*x += 10` writes a copy. Pattern-created mutable references are not wired to the original storage.

name: patterns_struct_bind
reduction: `let P{x:a,y:b}=p; a*b` yields 0 not 24. Field-to-new-name struct destructuring in a let binds a and b to 0; struct pattern field extraction with renamed bindings is broken.

name: patterns_tuple_nested
reduction: `let ((a,_),(_,d)) = ((1,2),(3,4)); a+d` yields 0 not 5. Nested tuple destructuring in a let binds inner elements to 0; only one level of tuple projection is handled.

name: patterns_struct_dotdot
feature: struct pattern with .. rest, let S{a,..}
reduction: `let S{a,..}=s;` then print a -> derived segfaults (139). The `..` rest in a struct pattern is mishandled, corrupting field-offset resolution and crashing at runtime.

name: patterns_slice
reduction: `match a { [first,..,last] => first+last }` on [1,2,3,4] segfaults (139). Slice/array subslice patterns with `..` are unsupported; the frontend emits code that dereferences bad offsets.

name: genenum_and_then
reduction: and_then ignores the closure's returned Option and yields the original inner value (4) instead of the mapped Some(40); combinator is a no-op.

name: genenum_filter
reduction: filter never applies the predicate (5 is odd -> should become None -> unwrap_or(-1)); returns original Some(5).

name: genenum_or
reduction: None.or(Some(9)) not substituted; unwrap on still-None panics (exit 101) instead of yielding 9.

name: genenum_get_or_insert
reduction: get_or_insert(8) on None does not insert; deref of returned ref reads 0 instead of 8.

name: genenum_map_err
reduction: map_err returns garbage (uninitialized/pointer-like 24117256); closure e+100 not applied to Err payload.

name: genenum_map_or
reduction: map_or(default, f) yields garbage instead of f(3)=4; two-arg default+closure combinator unimplemented.

name: genenum_ok_or_else
reduction: ok_or_else on None returns garbage; the else-closure error value 5 not produced.

name: genenum_unwrap_or_else
reduction: unwrap_or_else on None returns garbage rather than invoking the closure to get 42.

name: genenum_result_chain
reduction: half(8).and_then(half): derived stops at first result (4); and_then does not thread through second call (should be 2). Same and_then no-op as Option case.

name: genenum_generic_enum
reduction: Declaring `enum Maybe<T>{Just(T),Nothing}` hangs the frontend; generic-parameter enum decl not parsed (infinite loop).

name: genenum_generic_two
reduction: Two-type-param `enum Pair<A,B>` also hangs frontend; same generic-enum parse loop.

name: traits_default_override
feature: default method + override; empty impl uses default
reduction: A.v() where impl uses trait default (empty impl block) prints garbage const 0x1700008; direct trait-method dispatch on concrete receiver miscompiles

name: traits_supertrait
feature: supertrait Ext: Base, default calls supertrait required
reduction: S.plus() default in supertrait calling self.id() -> garbage const; concrete-receiver dispatch broken

name: traits_from_into
reduction: let m: Meters = x.into() segfaults (139); .into() dispatch through From impl not lowered

name: traits_from_direct
reduction: W::from(5) segfaults; From associated-fn call path crashes

name: traits_multi_bound
feature: multiple trait bounds T: A + B
reduction: f<T:A+B>(&S) segfaults; two-trait bound dispatch on &T crashes

name: traits_generic_method
feature: generic trait method fn conv<T: From<i64>>
reduction: T::from(8) inside generic method returns garbage const; generic-method + From miscompiles

name: traits_default_chain
reduction: S.b() chained defaults -> garbage const; concrete-receiver default dispatch broken

name: traits_assoc_const
feature: associated const in trait, default reads Self::ID
reduction: S.get() reading Self::ID -> garbage const; assoc const not materialized

name: traits_into_param
reduction: take(impl Into<C>) then v.into() segfaults; impl-Trait param + Into crashes

name: traits_default_self_field
reduction: isolated: a trait method returning self.0 on a tuple struct, called directly (S(6).s()), already miscompiles to garbage const; generic-bound path is fine

name: traits_supertrait_multi
reduction: S.z() default summing self.x()+self.y() from two supertraits -> garbage const

name: closures_fnmut
feature: FnMut mutating captured counter across calls
reduction: let mut c=0; let mut inc=||{c+=1;c}; three calls should yield 3, derived yields 1. FnMut mutation of a captured var is NOT persisted across invocations — the var is captured by value/copy each call rather than by &mut, so increments don't accumulate.

name: closures_capture_mut_state
feature: FnMut &mut capture accumulating in a loop
reduction: let mut sum=0; let mut add=|n|{sum+=n;}; sum after adding 1..=5 should be 15, derived gives 0. Same root cause as closures_fnmut: writes through a &mut captured var never reach the outer variable — captured-var mutation is dropped (outer sum stays at init 0).

name: closures_return_boxed
reduction: Box::new(|x| x*3) returned as Box<dyn Fn(i64)->i64>, then f(14) should give 42; derived returns garbage 24117268. Trait-object closure dispatch through a Box (vtable/fat-pointer call) is miscompiled — the call target/arg is a raw address, not the invoked closure.

name: closures_in_struct
feature: closure stored in generic struct field F: Fn
reduction: struct Holder<F: Fn(i64)->i64>{f:F}; calling (h.f)(23) hangs the derived binary (timeout). Monomorphized closure-typed struct field + call-through-field is unsupported — codegen loops/faults instead of dispatching.

name: closures_in_struct_box
feature: Box<dyn Fn> stored in struct field
reduction: struct H{f:Box<dyn Fn(i64)->i64>}; (h.f)(50) hangs. Trait-object closure in a struct field: call-through-field fat-pointer dispatch never terminates — same trait-object-closure weakness as closures_return_boxed but as a hang.

name: closures_unsound_movecap
reduction: let s=String::from("hi"); let f=move||s.len(); then s.len() again. rustc rejects (borrow of moved value s). Derived accepts and runs (prints 2 twice) — no move/ownership check on move-closure captures, so use-after-move is not diagnosed.

name: structs_mut_field
reduction: Minimal: `let mut s=S{x:1}; s.x += 41; println!(s.x)` -> derived prints 0, rustc 42. Plain `s.x = 41` works (41) and a local `n += 41` works (42); ONLY compound-assign to a struct FIELD is miscompiled (reads stale/zero, drops the add).

name: structs_self_mut
feature: &mut self method mutating a field with +=
reduction: Same root cause as structs_mut_field: `self.n += 1` inside &mut self compiles to a no-op/zero. Three inc() calls yield 0 instead of 3. Field compound-assignment broken.

name: structs_builder_self
feature: builder: `mut self` method returns Self after self.n += k
reduction: Reduces to the field compound-assign bug: `fn add(mut self,k){ self.n += k; self }`. Chained new().add(5).add(10) yields 0 not 15 because each `self.n += k` fails to update the field.

name: structs_shorthand
feature: field-init shorthand P{x,y} + struct returned by value from fn
reduction: Shorthand is NOT the cause: `P{x,y}` built inside main works (33). Real cause: returning a struct BY VALUE from a fn `fn mk(x,y)->P{P{x:x,y:y}}` then reading p.x+p.y yields garbage (24117256). By-value struct return miscompiles the returned aggregate.

name: structs_derive_default
reduction: `let s:S=Default::default(); s.a+s.b+99` -> derived 0, rustc 99. Explicit `S{a:0,b:0}` + `+99` gives 99 correctly, and bare `println!(99)` with the derive present gives 99. Cause: a struct produced by Default::default() is not a usable aggregate — subsequent field reads collapse the whole expression (incl. the +99 constant) to 0.

name: structs_update_syntax
reduction: Derived emits an ELF that segfaults (exit 139, no output) vs rustc 5. Same Default::default() cluster as structs_derive_default; the `..Default::default()` spread base is mishandled and corrupts the struct build, faulting at runtime.

name: ctrlflow_block_value
reduction: `let x = { 5+8 }; println!("{}",x)` -> derived prints nothing and leaks the block's value 13 into the process exit code. Confirmed minimal: `println!("{}", {5+8})` -> out=0 rc=13. A brace-delimited block in value position is not lowered as an rvalue; its trailing expression escapes to the exit path instead of feeding the consumer. Plain `if/else` and `match` in value position work, so the gap is specifically the bare `{ }` block-as-value.

name: ctrlflow_iflet_else
reduction: `let v = if let Some(x)=Some(7) { x*2 } else { -1 };` -> derived takes the else arm (-1). Plain `if let Some(x)=o { .. } else { .. }` used as a STATEMENT matches correctly (prints 7), and `if cond {a} else {b}` as a value works. So the defect is if-LET specifically when used in expression/value position: the pattern-match test is dropped and the else branch is always chosen.

name: ctrlflow_iflet_chain
reduction: Same root as ctrlflow_iflet_else: an `if let ... else if let ... else` chain in value position falls through every let-pattern arm to the final else (0). if-let-as-expression match tests are not emitted.

name: ctrlflow_match_return_arm
reduction: `match n { 0 => return 100, _ => {} }` then `n+1`: for f(0) derived ignores the arm's `return 100` and falls through to `n+1`=1; f(0)+f(5)=1+6=7 vs oracle 106. A `return` statement appearing as a match arm body is not honored as control flow.

name: ctrlflow_qmark_option
reduction: `let x = v.first()?; Some(x+10)` returns garbage. The `?` desugar on Option (unwrap-or-early-return + Some-wrap) is not correctly lowered; the bound value is uninitialized/garbage.

name: ctrlflow_qmark_none
reduction: Same `?`-on-Option lowering defect as ctrlflow_qmark_option; the None early-return branch is not produced, yielding garbage instead of the unwrap_or(-9) default.

name: ctrlflow_qmark_result
feature: ? operator in fn returning Result, str::parse
reduction: `let n: i32 = s.parse()?; Ok(n+1)` segfaults (exit 139, no output). `?` on a Result from str::parse is unsupported/miscompiled at runtime.

name: ctrlflow_whilelet_nested
reduction: Two nested `while let Some = pop()` loops over a vec-of-vecs segfault (exit 139). Single-level while-let works (ctrlflow_whilelet OK), so the failure is the nested Vec<Vec<_>> / inner-pop case.

name: ctrlflow_unsound_missing_arm
reduction: `match n { 1 => 10, 3 => 30 }` with no wildcard is a compile error under rustc (non-exhaustive). Derived accepts it and runs, returning garbage. No exhaustiveness check in the frontend.

name: ctrlflow_qmark_type_mismatch
feature: ? on Option in fn returning Result (type error)
reduction: `fn f(o:Option<i32>)->Result<i32,String>{ let x=o?; Ok(x) }` is rejected by rustc (Option's `?` needs From into the Result error type / no such impl). Derived accepts and runs. The `?` operator does no error-type / trait compatibility checking.

name: borrow_double_mut
reduction: borrow checker correctly rejects double &mut

name: borrow_use_after_move
reduction: no move-tracking for String let b=a; a still usable -> derived accepts invalid program

name: borrow_methodmut
reduction: c.inc() via &mut self does not persist self.n mutation; final self.n reads initial-derived 0 not 7

name: borrow_mutfield
reduction: bump(&mut p) mutation of p.x not written back; p.x reads 0 (whereas &mut i64 case works -> field-through-pointer store broken)

name: borrow_methodchain
reduction: c.add(3).add(4) returning self as &mut C -> infinite loop/hang in codegen of chained &mut Self return

name: borrow_retfield
reduction: *getx(&p) where getx returns &i64 segfaults; returning address-of-field mishandled

name: borrow_swap
reduction: std::mem::swap unsupported/unresolved -> no output, nonzero exit

name: borrow_swapfield
reduction: mem::swap of p.x/p.y not implemented

name: borrow_replace
reduction: std::mem::replace unsupported -> empty output

name: borrow_replace_struct
reduction: mem::replace(&mut p,P{..}) wrongly triggers move-of-p error; replace not modeled as non-consuming

name: borrow_take
reduction: std::mem::take unsupported

name: borrow_take_vec
reduction: mem::take of Vec unsupported

name: hashmap_get
reduction: m.get(&2) after m.insert(2,20) returns a garbage/pointer-like value (~0x1700...) not 20; scalar lookup broken while len/contains/entry-iter store correctly -> get retrieves address, not value.

name: hashmap_getmiss
reduction: get(&99) on empty map should yield None->-1; derived returns garbage then exit 139. Miss not detected by lookup.

name: hashmap_getmut
reduction: get_mut(&1) then *v+=7; m[&1] returns garbage pointer. Same scalar lookup returns address not stored i32.

name: hashmap_orinsert
reduction: *m.entry(1).or_insert(0)+=5 twice; m[&1] should be 8, derived garbage. or_insert deref-lookup returns address.

name: hashmap_orinsertwith
reduction: entry(7).or_insert_with(||42); *v should be 42, derived garbage pointer. Same deref-of-entry-slot bug.

name: hashmap_movekey
reduction: String-keyed m["a"] returns garbage; scalar value lookup bug independent of key type.

name: hashmap_overwrite
reduction: m.insert(1,99) should return Some(10); old.unwrap_or + m[&1] segfaults (139). insert-returns-old + lookup both fail.

name: hashmap_sumvals
reduction: for v in m.values() segfaults. values() iterator broken while &m entry-iteration works.

name: hashmap_sumkeys
reduction: for k in m.keys() segfaults. Dedicated keys()/values() views are the gap; entry-iter over &m works.

name: hashmap_valsmut
reduction: for v in m.values_mut() segfaults. Mutable value view unimplemented.

name: hashmap_count
reduction: *entry.or_insert(0)+=1 loop then m[&3] segfaults; broken scalar-index lookup under a loop.

name: hashset_basic
reduction: expected len(3)+contains(1)=4; derived prints 0 -> HashSet len==0 and contains false, backing non-functional.

name: recurse_deep
reduction: Derived toolchain segfaults on deep single-arg recursion. Bisected: count(1000) OK, count(2000) crashes (exit 139) -> threshold between 1000 and 2000 frames. Oracle handles 5000 fine. Consistent with the fixed frame-base memory model (frame base 0x2000000): recursion frames collide/overflow the arena well before rustc's real stack limit. Real rung: limited/fixed call-stack region in cf backend.

name: recurse_undefined_call
reduction: Calling an undeclared fn `ghost(3)` is a compile error in rustc (E0425) but the derived frontend accepts it and emits a program that prints 0 and exits 0. Minimal: `fn main(){ println!("{}", ghost(3)); }`. Frontend does no name-resolution check for callee existence -> unresolved call lowers to a 0-returning stub instead of a hard error.

name: operators_neg
reduction: -N(5) via user Neg impl: derived produces an ELF that SIGSEGVs (exit 139) instead of returning -5. Unary operator-overload dispatch for a user Neg impl is broken (crashes).

name: operators_index
reduction: a[2]->8 (should be 9), a[1]->7, a[0]->garbage(24117260). User Index impl is off-by-one: a[i] deref reads element i-1 with a[0] reading out of bounds. The &self.d[i] reference return through the overloaded index is mis-lowered.

name: operators_addassign
reduction: a starts v=5 (prints 5 correctly), a+=C{v:3} yields 0 not 8. The overloaded += on a struct is not dispatched to add_assign; the compound-assign path zeroes/discards the value.

name: operators_ord_tuplecmp
reduction: P{x:2,y:1} > P{x:1,y:9}: x is decisive (2>1) so true, but derived gives 0. Derived Ord derive does not compare fields lexicographically correctly (ignores/misorders the first field or falls through to y).

name: operators_bad_noimpl
reduction: a==b on a struct with no PartialEq impl: rustc rejects (E0369), derived accepts and runs (prints 0). Frontend does no trait-bound check for == operands.

name: fmt_bin
reduction: println!("{:b}",42) - the 'b' spec is ignored; value printed as plain decimal.

name: fmt_oct
reduction: println!("{:o}",42) - 'o' spec ignored, plain decimal emitted.

name: fmt_hexup
reduction: println!("{:X}",255) - only lowercase {:x} is handled; {:X} falls through to decimal.

name: fmt_altx
reduction: '#' alternate flag ignored: no 0x prefix emitted (base hex still applied).

name: fmt_altb
reduction: both '#' and 'b' ignored; plain decimal 5 emitted.

name: fmt_plus
reduction: '+' sign flag ignored; positive value printed without leading '+'.

name: fmt_signhex
reduction: '+' flag dropped; hex applied but no sign prefix.

name: fmt_prec
reduction: println!("{:.3}",42) - precision '.3' misparsed as width 3, right-padding to ' 42' instead of being ignored (rustc ignores precision for integers).

name: fmt_width_arg
reduction: println!("{:1$}",5,4) - the '1$' width-from-arg reference is not resolved; no padding applied.

name: fmt_exp
reduction: println!("{:e}",1000) - 'e' scientific spec ignored, plain decimal emitted.

name: fmt_dbg_tuple
reduction: println!("{:?}",(1,2,3)) - tuple Debug unimplemented; prints a raw pointer/garbage int instead of (1, 2, 3).

name: fmt_dbg_vec
reduction: println!("{:?}",vec![1,2,3]) - Vec Debug unimplemented; prints raw pointer value, not [1, 2, 3].

name: fmt_dbg_nested
reduction: Debug of a Vec of structs: prints a single struct with a garbage field instead of iterating the vec - nested/aggregate Debug not composed.

name: fmt_neg_hex
reduction: println!("{:x}",-1i8) - should two's-complement to ff; derived emits a single char '/' (0x2F), hex-of-negative path corrupt.

name: consts_const_fn
feature: const fn call evaluated in const initializer
reduction: const V = sq(7) where sq is const fn -> prints 0; a const initialized by a const-fn call is not evaluated, folds to 0. Plain arithmetic consts (const_ref_const) work, so the gap is const-fn evaluation in const context.

name: consts_nested_const_fn
feature: nested const fn calls in const initializer
reduction: same root as consts_const_fn: const-fn-initialized const yields 0.

name: consts_const_arr_n
feature: const [i64;N] array with const N, indexed
reduction: const A:[i64;5]=[..]; A[3] prints 0; const array data is not emitted/read, indexing yields 0.

name: consts_const_expr_len
reduction: [7;N] with const N=2+3 -> a[0] reads 0 and/or len wrong; local const-sized array literal not materialized.

name: consts_const_fn_array
feature: const array whose elements are const-fn calls
reduction: combines const-array + const-fn-element bugs; all elements read 0.

name: consts_static_table
reduction: static T:[i64;4]=[3,5,7,9]; runtime sum -> 0; static array initializer data not placed/read, every element 0.

name: consts_static_idx_runtime
feature: static array indexed by runtime arg in a fn
reduction: T[i] via fn(i) -> 0; same static-array-data-not-emitted root.

name: consts_static_mut_like
feature: static array sized by const, summed over const bound
reduction: same static-array data root; SQUARES[i] all read 0.

name: consts_const_in_match
feature: const values used as match arm patterns
reduction: x=9 should hit HI=>200 but derived prints 100 (LO arm): a const identifier in a match arm is treated as a catch-all binding pattern (irrefutable) rather than a const comparison, so the first arm always matches.

name: consts_assoc_const_self
feature: associated const on struct via Self::K
reduction: impl C { const K:i64=42; } Self::K -> 0; associated const not resolved to its value.

name: consts_assoc_const_generic
feature: associated const on a generic type param (T::MAX)
reduction: m::<A>()+m::<B>() prints 'true' not 33; T::MAX on a generic param resolves to a bogus (bool-typed) value, generic assoc-const dispatch broken.

name: consts_enum_discrim_default
feature: enum discriminant default value (E::D as i64)
reduction: enum E{A,B,C,D}; E::D as i64 -> garbage 24117256 instead of 3; default discriminant sequencing not implemented, `as i64` casts a raw variant handle/pointer.

name: consts_enum_discrim
reduction: minimal 'enum E { A = 5 }' hangs the frontend (rc=124); the `Variant = <expr>` discriminant syntax is not parsed and sends the parser into an infinite loop. 'enum E { A }' parses fine.

name: consts_enum_discrim_expr
feature: enum discriminant from const expr (A = K, B = K+4)
reduction: same parser hang as consts_enum_discrim: any `Variant = ...` discriminant loops the frontend.

name: consts_unsound_oob
reduction: const X = A[5] on [i64;3] is a compile error in rustc (index out of bounds); derived accepts it and prints 0 — no const-eval bounds checking (consistent with const arrays folding to 0).

name: convert_bad_charcast
reduction: `n as char` where n:i64 is rejected by rustc (only u8 may cast to char); derived accepts it and prints 65 -> no cast-legality check

name: convert_float_to_int
reduction: `3.9_f64 as i64` produces an ELF that segfaults (exit 139); float->int truncation cast unsupported in codegen

name: convert_from_impl
reduction: user From impl / Cel::from associated call crashes (139); trait-based From not resolved

name: convert_into
reduction: `21i64.into()` for a user From<i64> crashes (139); Into blanket-impl resolution absent

name: convert_int_to_float
reduction: `7 as f64 / 2.0` yields 3 not 3.5; `as f64` is a no-op, value stays integer and division is integer division

name: convert_narrow_trunc
reduction: 0x1_0000_0001 as u32 keeps all 64 bits; narrowing cast does not mask to 32 bits (no width tracking, everything is i64)

name: convert_suffix_lit
reduction: 100u8.wrapping_add(200u8) gives 300 not 44; literal width suffix ignored, arithmetic done at i64 width with no u8 wrap

name: convert_tryfrom
reduction: u8::try_from(300i64).is_err() crashes (139); TryFrom + Result path unsupported

name: convert_u32_to_char
reduction: println! of a char prints its codepoint 66 instead of 'B'; char Display formats as integer, not the character

name: nestgen_vecvec
reduction: expected 15; r.iter().sum() over an inner Vec obtained from outer .iter() yields a pointer value, not the sum. Nested iterator adaptor over Vec<Vec<T>> mishandles the inner element type (Vec vs value).

name: nestgen_vectuple
reduction: expected 14; iterating a Vec of tuples and destructuring &(a,b) in the closure yields garbage. Tuple element loads inside map over a Vec use wrong offset/stride.

name: nestgen_vecvecstr
reduction: expected 3, got 2; sum of inner .len() over Vec<Vec<&str>> undercounts (last inner row's len dropped) in nested iteration.

name: nestgen_genret
feature: generic fn returning Option<T>, then unwrap().len()
reduction: expected 3; wrap(vec![..]) -> Some(vec) monomorphized with T=Vec, then unwrap().len() returns a pointer. Generic Some(T) with T=Vec loses the vec header so .len() reads garbage.

name: nestgen_optopt
reduction: expected 42; Option<Option<i32>>.flatten() then unwrap returns pointer garbage. Nested Option flatten not lowered / inner payload offset wrong.

name: nestgen_structvecs
reduction: expected 5; r.cells.len() over Vec<Row> where Row holds a Vec field returns a pointer. Field-of-Vec .len() inside iter().map is miscompiled.

name: nestgen_veccollect
reduction: expected 9; collect into Vec<Vec<i32>> then flatten().sum yields pointer garbage. Either collect of Vec-valued items or flatten over nested Vec is wrong.

name: nestgen_vecopt
reduction: expected 4; filter_map over Vec<Option<i32>> deref of the Option element returns garbage sum. Option element load/unwrap in the adaptor is wrong.

name: nestgen_vecresult
reduction: expected 3; Result::ok() inside filter_map over a Vec of Results yields pointer garbage. Result payload/discriminant handling in adaptor is wrong.

name: nestgen_hmvec
reduction: expected 12; HashMap with Vec values via entry/or_insert_with then indexed .iter().sum returns pointer. Vec-valued HashMap slot read miscompiled.

name: nestgen_optvec
reduction: expected 60; SEGV (139). Option<Vec>.map closure summing the inner Vec crashes; unwrapping a Vec-payload Option inside map dereferences a bad pointer.

name: nestgen_hmveciter
reduction: expected 12; SEGV (139). Iterating m.values() (Vec items) then inner for over each Vec crashes; nested iteration over HashMap Vec-values dereferences a bad pointer.

name: misc_arr_destructure
reduction: let [a,b]=[10,20]; println!(a) prints 0 while a[0] indexing works (prints 10). Array/slice pattern in a let binding is not lowered; all bound names read 0.

name: misc_tuple_destructure
reduction: Flat let (a,b)=(10,20) works, but nested let (a,(b,c))=(1,(2,3)) makes b/c read 0. Nested/recursive tuple patterns not destructured.

name: misc_slice_pat_bind
feature: slice pattern with .. rest: if let [first,..,last]
reduction: if let [first,..,last]=a produces empty output; middle-rest slice pattern binding unsupported.

name: misc_slice_rest
reduction: rest @ .. binding in an array let pattern; same root as array destructuring, bound names read 0.

name: misc_labeled_continue
reduction: Unlabeled continue works; labeled `continue 'o` does not target the outer loop, inner iterations not skipped, sum is 66 not 30.

name: misc_labeled_break_val
reduction: loop { break 'l 99 } as expression yields 108 instead of 99; labeled break value not propagated as the loop's value.

name: misc_nested_closure
feature: nested closure returning closure (curry) |a| move |b| a+b
reduction: Closure returning a move closure yields a garbage large value (pointer-class), captured environment not applied. Higher-order closure returns unsupported.

name: misc_chain_iter_fold
reduction: vec!/.iter().map().fold garbage (~24M, same pointer-class value as nested closure); Vec iterator with map+fold not evaluated to a real sum.
